import os
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Dynamically locate dataset path relative to script/notebook location
BASE_DIR = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == 'notebooks' else Path.cwd()
DATA_PATH = BASE_DIR / 'data' / 'Video_Games_Sales_as_at_22_Dec_2016.csv'

# Check if file exists to prevent path errors
if not DATA_PATH.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Could not find dataset at: {DATA_PATH.resolve()}")

# 1. Load Dataset
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

# Data Cleaning
df['Year_of_Release'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Year_of_Release'], errors='coerce')
df['User_Score'] = pd.to_numeric(df['User_Score'], errors='coerce')
df = df.dropna(subset=['Year_of_Release', 'Genre', 'Publisher', 'Global_Sales'])
df['Year_of_Release'] = df['Year_of_Release'].astype(int)

# --- QUESTION 1: Regional Shift Over Time ---
regional_sales = df[(df['Year_of_Release'] >= 1990) & (df['Year_of_Release'] <= 2016)].groupby('Year_of_Release')[['NA_Sales', 'EU_Sales', 'JP_Sales']].sum().reset_index()

fig1 = go.Figure()
fig1.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=regional_sales['Year_of_Release'], y=regional_sales['NA_Sales'], mode='lines', name='North America', line=dict(color='#2b5c8f', width=3)))
fig1.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=regional_sales['Year_of_Release'], y=regional_sales['EU_Sales'], mode='lines', name='Europe', line=dict(color='#d95f02', width=3)))
fig1.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=regional_sales['Year_of_Release'], y=regional_sales['JP_Sales'], mode='lines', name='Japan', line=dict(color='#7570b3', width=2)))

fig1.update_layout(
    title='<b>North America and Europe Dominated Global Expansion Post-2000 While Japan Remained Flat</b>',
    xaxis_title='Year of Release',
    yaxis_title='Total Sales (Millions)',
    template='plotly_white',
    hovermode='x unified'
)
fig1.show()

# --- QUESTION 2: Genre Performance Across Regions ---
genre_reg = df.groupby('Genre')[['NA_Sales', 'JP_Sales']].sum().reset_index()
genre_reg['JP_NA_Ratio'] = genre_reg['JP_Sales'] / genre_reg['NA_Sales']
genre_reg = genre_reg.sort_values('JP_NA_Ratio', ascending=True)

fig2 = px.bar(
    genre_reg, y='Genre', x=['NA_Sales', 'JP_Sales'],
    barmode='group',
    title='<b>Role-Playing Games Outperform in Japan, Whereas Action/Shooters Rule North America</b>',
    labels={'value': 'Sales (Millions)', 'variable': 'Region'},
    color_discrete_map={'NA_Sales': '#2b5c8f', 'JP_Sales': '#d95f02'}
)
fig2.update_layout(template='plotly_white', yaxis={'categoryorder':'total ascending'})
fig2.show()

# --- QUESTION 3: Critic vs. User Score Impact on Sales ---
scored_df = df.dropna(subset=['Critic_Score', 'User_Score']).copy()
fig3 = px.scatter(
    scored_df, x='Critic_Score', y='Global_Sales', color='Genre',
    size='User_Score', hover_data=['Name', 'Platform'],
    title='<b>High Critic Ratings (>80) Strongly Correlate with Blockbuster Sales Success</b>',
    labels={'Critic_Score': 'Critic Score (0-100)', 'Global_Sales': 'Global Sales (Millions)'}
)
fig3.update_layout(template='plotly_white')
fig3.show()

# --- QUESTION 4: Platform Wars (Sony vs. Microsoft vs. Nintendo) ---
def get_company(platform):
    if platform in ['PS', 'PS2', 'PS3', 'PS4', 'PSP', 'PSV']: return 'Sony'
    elif platform in ['XB', 'X360', 'XOne']: return 'Microsoft'
    elif platform in ['NES', 'SNES', 'N64', 'GC', 'Wii', 'WiiU', 'GB', 'GBA', 'DS', '3DS']: return 'Nintendo'
    return 'Other'

df['Company'] = df['Platform'].apply(get_company)
comp_sales = df[df['Company'] != 'Other'].groupby(['Year_of_Release', 'Company'])['Global_Sales'].sum().reset_index()

fig4 = px.line(
    comp_sales, x='Year_of_Release', y='Global_Sales', color='Company',
    title='<b>Nintendo Peak in 2006 (Wii) Outpaced Competitors Before Sony Reclaimed Market Share</b>',
    color_discrete_map={'Sony': '#2b5c8f', 'Nintendo': '#d95f02', 'Microsoft': '#1b9e77'}
)
fig4.update_layout(template='plotly_white')
fig4.show()

# --- QUESTION 5: Sales Lifespan of Hardware Platforms ---
top_platforms = df.groupby('Platform')['Global_Sales'].sum().nlargest(10).index
plat_df = df[df['Platform'].isin(top_platforms)]

fig5 = px.box(
    plat_df, x='Platform', y='Global_Sales', color='Platform',
    title='<b>PS2 and DS Generated the Highest Concentration of Multi-Million Unit Titles</b>',
    labels={'Global_Sales': 'Global Sales (Millions)'},
    log_y=True
)
fig5.update_layout(template='plotly_white', showlegend=False)
fig5.show()

# --- QUESTION 6: Developer Rating Discrepancies ---
top_pub = df['Publisher'].value_counts().head(8).index
pub_df = df[df['Publisher'].isin(top_pub)].dropna(subset=['Critic_Score', 'User_Score'])
pub_scores = pub_df.groupby('Publisher')[['Critic_Score', 'User_Score']].mean().reset_index()
pub_scores['User_Score_Scaled'] = pub_scores['User_Score'] * 10

fig6 = go.Figure()
fig6.add_trace(go.Bar(x=pub_scores['Publisher'], y=pub_scores['Critic_Score'], name='Critic Score', marker_color='#2b5c8f'))
fig6.add_trace(go.Bar(x=pub_scores['Publisher'], y=pub_scores['User_Score_Scaled'], name='User Score (x10)', marker_color='#cccccc'))
fig6.update_layout(
    barmode='group',
    title='<b>Publishers Experience Higher Disparity Between Official Critic Reviews and User Ratings</b>',
    template='plotly_white'
)
fig6.show()

# --- QUESTION 7: ESRB Rating Distribution by Global Market ---
esrb_df = df.dropna(subset=['Rating']).groupby('Rating')[['NA_Sales', 'EU_Sales', 'JP_Sales']].sum().reset_index()

fig7 = px.bar(
    esrb_df, x='Rating', y=['NA_Sales', 'EU_Sales', 'JP_Sales'],
    title='<b>"Everyone" (E) and "Mature" (M) Ratings Account for the Majority of Revenue</b>',
    labels={'value': 'Sales (Millions)', 'variable': 'Region'},
    color_discrete_sequence=['#2b5c8f', '#d95f02', '#7570b3']
)
fig7.update_layout(template='plotly_white')
fig7.show()

# --- QUESTION 8: Release Density vs Average Sales per Game ---
yearly_perf = df.groupby('Year_of_Release').agg(
    Total_Games=('Name', 'count'),
    Avg_Sales=('Global_Sales', 'mean')
).reset_index()

fig8 = px.scatter(
    yearly_perf, x='Total_Games', y='Avg_Sales', text='Year_of_Release',
    title='<b>Market Saturation: Higher Game Release Density Reduces Average Units Sold per Game</b>',
    labels={'Total_Games': 'Number of Games Released', 'Avg_Sales': 'Average Sales per Game (M)'}
)
fig8.update_traces(textposition='top center', marker=dict(size=10, color='#2b5c8f'))
fig8.update_layout(template='plotly_white')
fig8.show()

# --- QUESTION 9: Genre Evolution Over Decades ---
df['Decade'] = pd.cut(df['Year_of_Release'], bins=[1979, 1989, 1999, 2009, 2020], labels=['1980s', '1990s', '2000s', '2010s'])
decade_genre = df.groupby(['Decade', 'Genre'], observed=False)['Global_Sales'].sum().reset_index()

fig9 = px.bar(
    decade_genre, x='Decade', y='Global_Sales', color='Genre',
    title='<b>Action and Sports Overtook Platformers and RPGs as Dominant Revenue Drivers Post-2000</b>',
    labels={'Global_Sales': 'Global Sales (Millions)'}
)
fig9.update_layout(template='plotly_white')
fig9.show()

# --- QUESTION 10: Top Franchise Hit Concentration ---
top_games = df.nlargest(15, 'Global_Sales')

fig10 = px.bar(
    top_games, x='Global_Sales', y='Name', color='Platform', orientation='h',
    title='<b>Wii Sports and Super Mario Bros. Stand as Historical Outliers in Global Sales Volume</b>',
    labels={'Global_Sales': 'Global Sales (Millions)', 'Name': 'Game Title'}
)
fig10.update_layout(template='plotly_white', yaxis={'categoryorder':'total ascending'})
fig10.show()
